section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the superiority of Pesach Sheni over Pesach Rishon lies not only in the higher place from which its leap is drawn, but also in the leap itself being of a higher quality.
section.t: And one may add,
that the superiority of Pesach Sheni relative to Pesach Rishon is not only that the leap of Pesach Sheni is drawn from a more elevated place,
but also that the leap itself is a more elevated leap.
And this is also understood from the fact that it is called "Pesach Sheni,"
for the simple explanation of "Pesach Sheni" is not
(only)
that the Pesach
(the leap)
is drawn in the level of "second," but rather that
(also)
the Pesach
(the leap)
is "second,"
a leap more elevated than the leap of Pesach Rishon.
And what is stated in the maamar, that the explanation of "Pesach Sheni" is that the leap of Pesach Sheni is drawn in the level of "second"
(Yesod),
is
because the superiority of the leap of Pesach Sheni
(that the leap is more elevated)
is seen
(also)
in that the leap is drawn in the level of "second"
(as will be explained in section 5).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the Tzemach Tzedek's explanation of Pesach Sheni as a second and higher level of service with the simple meaning of Pesach Sheni as a correction for those who did not offer the Pesach, because its revelation is a leap beyond all measure.
section.t: And based on this, one can connect the above explanation
(of the Tzemach Tzedek)
that Pesach Sheni is a second and elevated level in the service that comes after the preparatory service of Pesach Rishon,
with the concept of Pesach Sheni as it is simply understood,
that it is a correction and completion for one who did not offer the Pesach,
because the fact that Pesach Sheni corrects and completes the lack of the one who did not offer the Pesach is because the revelation of Pesach Sheni is a leap that is not according to order,
which has no measurements or limitations,
not even the measurements and limitations of the leap of Pesach
(Rishon),
and regarding this revelation – "nothing is lost."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the primary service of the Sefirah of Yesod (the second month) is not the refinement of the animal soul but the drawing down of the 49 Gates of Binah, culminating in the Fiftieth Gate, paralleling the Avot as the Merkavah.
section.t: And this will be understood by prefacing the known concept
that among the distinctions between Zeir Anpin and Malchut is,
that Malchut is the upper edge
(source)
of BY"A,
and Zeir Anpin is the lower edge of Atzilut.
And since in Atzilut "evil shall not sojourn,"
it is understood that this, that through Yesod
(Zeir Anpin)
the completion of the refinement is accomplished,
the matter of transformation,
is as it is drawn to refine,
and the primary service from the aspect of Zeir Anpin is
(not the matter of refinements,
but rather)
to draw down light.
And as it is regarding the Sefirah of Yesod
(its concept being the second month among the Sefirot),
so too is it regarding the service of Sefirat HaOmer
(its concept being the second month in the service of man),
that its primary matter
(according to one explanation)
is not the refinement of the attributes of the animal soul, but rather the drawing down of the 49 Gates of Binah,
until that through this the Fiftieth Gate is also drawn.
And it can be said,
that this is also what [the fact that] Iyar is an acronym for Avraham, Yitzchak, Yaakov, Rachel,
who are the four legs of the Merkavah,

that the self-nullification of the Merkavah is in a manner that from the outset there is no place for the matter of yeshut (selfhood), and certainly not for evil that requires one to effect its nullification,
as explained in Tanya
regarding the matter that the Avot are the Merkavah,
that they did not become a Merkavah except for the supernal will alone, all their days.
